issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), and the template's Main.java also references 'Milkable'. However, the provided solution introduces a different interface named 'Dairy' (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) which defines messageOnMilk(), while solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java is empty. Several solution classes (Seal.java, Goat.java) implement Dairy instead of Milkable. This name/type mismatch between 'Milkable' and 'Dairy' is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the intended interface name and API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (or vice versa update the problem/template), ensure Milkable.java declares the method String messageOnMilk(), and update Seal.java and Goat.java to implement Milkable. Remove any empty or duplicate Milkable/Dairy files so the interface name matches the UML and template references.

issues.description: The exercise and template expect an interface named 'Milkable' (used in the UML and referenced in Main.java), but the solution implements an interface named 'Dairy' with the same method (messageOnMilk). This naming divergence (Milkable vs Dairy) breaks the direct mapping between the problem statement/template and the solution implementation and can confuse students about which interface to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (update file name to Milkable.java and all implementations to 'implements Milkable'), or alternatively add a Milkable interface that delegates to Dairy so the template/problem and solution use the same identifier.
